learn.title: Waves
learn.body: Plot $\sin x$ against $x$ in radians and you get a smooth wave that repeats every $2\pi$. It starts at 0 and rises. The graph of $\cos x$ is the same wave starting at its peak, 1.

learn.title: The general form
learn.body: For $y=A\sin(Bx)+D$: the amplitude is $|A|$, the period is $\frac{2\pi}{B}$, and the midline is $y=D$. The wave swings from $D-|A|$ to $D+|A|$. A shift inside, $\sin(x-c)$, moves the graph right by $c$.

learn.title: Describe $y=3\sin(2x)$
steps: Midline $y=0$, so the wave runs from $-3$ to $3$

learn.title: Range of $y=2\cos x+1$
learn.body: Add the midline to the swing.
A bigger $B$ squeezes the wave, so the period gets shorter.

questions.prompt: What is the amplitude of $y=-5\sin x$?
questions.explanation: Amplitude is $|A|=5$. The minus sign flips the wave but not its height.

questions.prompt: Sketch $y=2\sin x+1$. Put the steps in order.
steps: Start at the midline and rise
questions.explanation: Midline first, then the swing, then the shape.
